scenes.heading: Working with first-time buyers vs. experienced investors

sents.d: Working with first-time buyers vs. experienced investors
These are two different client relationships that need two different approaches.

A first-time buyer typically needs more education and hand-holding through each step of the process, while an experienced investor usually wants efficient, direct communication and expects you to already know they understand the basics — treating both the same way frustrates each.

Setting realistic expectations early with first-time buyers (timeline, what's normal to feel nervous about, what actually matters vs. what doesn't) reduces anxiety-driven decision-making later in the process.

With investors, understanding their specific investment criteria (cash flow targets, property type, area) upfront saves both of you time by not showing properties that don't fit their actual strategy.

take: Educate first-time buyers; be direct and criteria-driven with investors.
